caseName: Heather Biddle, et al. v. The Walt Disney Company
summary: A proposed $50 million partial settlement concerns qualifying YouTube TV and DirecTV streaming subscriptions during the stated class period.
eligibilitySummary: Potentially applies only if you purchased YouTube TV or DirecTV Stream, DirecTV Now, or AT&T TV Now between April 1, 2019 and March 31, 2026, subject to the official notice and applicable state-law class definitions.
proofSummary: Online filing starts with the Unique ID and PIN from the mailed or emailed notice; the administrator can assist if a notice was not received or was lost. The form must be completed truthfully and may be validated against provider data.
estimatedBenefit: Pro rata cash payment based on qualifying subscription length; no individual amount is stated.
geography: United States; state-law class definitions and exclusions apply
court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
relevanceReason: Broad consumer subscription category; confirm service, dates, and state coverage.

caseName: Jones, et al. v. Lands' End, Inc.
summary: A proposed settlement concerns U.S. residents whose private information was compromised in the December 2024 Lands' End data incident.
eligibilitySummary: Potentially applies only if your private information was compromised in the December 2024 incident. A mailed or emailed notice is a strong signal, but the administrator must resolve eligibility.
proofSummary: The expected $60 alternate cash option states no proof or explanation is required; documented-loss claims up to $5,000 require supporting records. A settlement notice or administrator confirmation may be needed to establish class membership.
estimatedBenefit: Expected $60 alternate cash payment, or documented losses up to $5,000; two years of credit monitoring also offered.
court: Circuit Court for Iowa County, Wisconsin
relevanceReason: Nationwide consumer data incident; relevant only after confirming notice or affected status.

caseName: In re ZF-TRW Airbag Control Units Products Liability Litigation
summary: A finalized settlement offers benefits to eligible current and former owners or lessees of listed Toyota vehicles.
eligibilitySummary: Potentially applies only to current or former owners or lessees, as of July 31, 2023, of specified 2011-2019 Toyota models. The official VIN lookup determines whether a vehicle is included.
proofSummary: Vehicle eligibility requires the official VIN lookup. Expense reimbursement needs receipts, invoices, or a signed affidavit; never save a VIN in this dashboard.
estimatedBenefit: Eligible recall expenses may be reimbursed; potential residual distribution is up to $250, plus specified warranty or inspection benefits.
geography: United States, District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and U.S. territories
court: U.S. District Court, Central District of California
relevanceReason: Potentially high vehicle value, but only for specific Toyota models and verified VINs.

eligibilitySummary: Potentially applies only if you are a qualifying current or former Clark County, Washington resident whose personal information was involved in the incident.
proofSummary: Review the official notice and claim form for the selected benefit. Do not proceed unless the Clark County connection and affected status are truthful.
estimatedBenefit: Benefit varies by claim type; the official notice controls.
relevanceReason: Verified and open, but unlikely to fit a Texas household without a prior Clark County connection.

eligibilitySummary: Potentially applies only if you paid any amount for retail Chantix in the U.S. or its territories during the class period. This dashboard does not file claims or decide eligibility.

estimatedBenefit: Consumer payments are pro rata and capped; each consumer claim will not exceed the total amount paid for Chantix. No individual amount is guaranteed.
